nodes.question: What were the performance outcomes when merging models from distinct datasets and architectures in the experiments conducted?
nodes.answer: The experiments demonstrated performance improvements of up to 6.8% in mIoU for merging different-architecture models with a shared backbone and increased speed by 3.25 times when incorporating high-performing models into faster ones.

nodes.question: What performance improvements were observed in UDA when merging models from different datasets and architectures?
nodes.answer: Substantial UDA improvements included a 2.6% mean IoU (mIoU) increase for same-architecture models from distinct datasets and a 6.8% increase for different-architecture models with a shared backbone.

nodes.question: How does the model merging method improve performance in UDA according to the research findings?
nodes.answer: The model merging method demonstrates improvements in UDA performance with increases of 2.6% mIoU for same-architecture models from distinct datasets, and up to 6.8% mIoU for different-architecture models with a shared backbone, as well as a 7% increase in mPQ for merging semantic and panoptic segmentation models.

nodes.question: What are the reported performance improvements when merging same-architecture and different-architecture models, according to the experimental results?
nodes.answer: The report states a 2.6% mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) improvement when merging same-architecture models from distinct datasets, and a 6.8% mIoU improvement when merging different-architecture models with a shared backbone.
